title: Identification and analysis of the DNA content of small extracellular vesicles isolated from Leishmania parasites
protocol: Transfer 50 mL of late-log phase parasite culture to ten 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1000 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatants and add an additional 50 mL of culture to each tube.
Centrifuge again at 1000 × g for 5 minutes to concentrate parasites.
Remove supernatants and fill each tube with 50 mL of 1× PBS, then resuspend pellet by pipetting.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1000 × g for 5 minutes to wash parasites.
Repeat step to wash parasites again.
Resuspend concentrated parasites in 10 mL of RPMI-1640 medium without FBS and phenol red at a final concentration of 10^8 parasites/mL.
Transfer content of each tube to a single non-ventilated 25 cm² culture flask for each tube.
Incubate the concentrated parasites for 4 hours at 37°C with low agitation speed (less than 40 rpm).
Evaluate parasite viability using propidium iodide before and after the 4-hour incubation.
Collect 200 μL of parasites before and after the incubation.
Add PI at a final concentration of 50 μg/mL.
Pass the cells through a flow cytometer.
Centrifuge the samples at 1000 × g at 21°C for 5 min.
Transfer the supernatant to new 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the samples again at 1000 × g.
Recover and filter the supernatant using a 20 mL syringe and a 0.45 μm filter.
Repeat filtering using a 0.22 μm syringe filter and a new 20 mL syringe.
Distribute the filtered supernatant into ultracentrifuge tubes.
Fill the tubes with ice-cold exosome buffer, leaving about 1–2 cm of empty space.
Balance the tubes in pairs using an electronic scale, ensuring that opposite tubes are within 0.01 g.
Centrifuge the balanced tubes at 4°C for 1 hour at 100,000 × g using a SW 32 Ti Swinging-Bucket Rotor in the Beckman Coulter Optima L-100 XP ultracentrifuge.
Remove supernatants carefully with a pipette gun and 5 mL serological pipettes without disturbing the pellet, leaving about 200–300 μL of buffer in each tube.
Repeat the supernatant removal process two more times to complete three rounds of pipetting.
Gently resuspend the EV pellet using a P200 pipette with filter tips in the remaining 200–300 μL and pool the volumes into one single tube.
Fill the pooled tube with exosome buffer, leaving about 1–2 cm of empty space, and balance it using a tube filled with exosome buffer.
Centrifuge the balanced tubes for an additional hour at 100,000 × g and 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant, leaving small EVs in a single pellet in about 200–300 μL of exosome buffer.
Resuspend the small EV pellet using a P200 pipette with low retention filter tips in the remaining 200–300 μL exosome buffer.
Save 10 μL of EVs for protein quantification in low-binding microtubes.
Save 10 μL of EVs for nanoparticle tracking analysis in low-binding microtubes.
Save 10 μL of EVs for transmission electron microscopy in low-binding microtubes.
Aliquot 100 μL of remaining EV volume per microtube.
Freeze EVs at -80°C until needed.
Slowly thaw on ice the 10 μL EV aliquots reserved for protein quantification.
Dilute each aliquot by a factor of 1:20 using ultrapure water to facilitate EV lysis and protein release.
Quantify the EV protein using MicroBCA™ Protein assay kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Set the shutter frame rate to 45 and sensitivity to 85 according to the system’s software guidance.
Verify the accuracy of the ZetaView using 100 nm standard beads before sample measurements.
Slowly thaw on ice the 10 μL EV aliquots reserved for NTA.
Dilute the samples in 0.22 μm filtered exosome buffer with a dilution factor of 1:1,000 to 1:10,000 to achieve a particle count between 1,000 and 2,000.
Run each sample at 25°C to measure particle size and concentration.
Report the EV diameter distribution rather than summarizing as a single metric.
Using a pipette, add side-by-side onto a clean piece of parafilm:
Add 1 drop (10 μl) of 2.5% glutaraldehyde.
Add 3 drops of distilled water.
Add 1 drop of 1% uranyl acetate.
Gently pick up a 200 mesh Cu TEM grid with carbon support using precision tweezers.
Glow discharge the grid before use to clean and enhance sample binding.
Add 5 μL of EV sample to the carbon side of the grid using a micropipette.
Let sit for 1 min.
Dry excess sample by touching the side of the grid to filter paper or Kimwipe.
Place the grid carbon-side down on the glutaraldehyde droplet for 1 min to fix the sample.
Wash the grid by placing it carbon-side down on each water droplet for 1 min, repeating three times in total.
Place the grid, carbon-side down, on the uranyl acetate droplet for 1 min to stain the sample.
Dry the excess uranyl acetate by touching the side of the grid to filter paper or Kimwipe.
Allow the grid to air dry for 30 min on its holder.
Use the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit from QIAGEN to extract EV-associated DNA from one aliquot of purified EVs, following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the columns with 100 μL of elution buffer.
Optionally treat purified EVs with TURBO DNase for 30 minutes to degrade DNA outside the vesicles before purifying the DNA.
Further concentrate the DNA using a SpeedVac Concentrator with low-binding tubes if needed.
Quantify the purified DNA using the Quant-iT PicoGreen dsDNA Assay Kit in a Take 3 platform or other instruments.
Store the DNA at -20°C until ready for next-generation sequencing library preparation.
Construct EV DNA libraries using the KAPA HyperPrep kit without fragmentation.
Determine the number of PCR cycles for library amplification by qPCR, typically ranging between 10-15 cycles based on input DNA amount.
Run an aliquot of each library on a Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA Assay chip to confirm fragment size distribution.
Ensure that the DNA fragment size from EVs mostly ranges from 200-500 bp.
Assess the sequencing quality using FastQC.
Run FastQC on raw sequence files in FASTQ format.
Trim the sequencing adapters and low-quality bases using Trimmomatic.
Create an index of the Leishmania infantum reference genome assembly using Bowtie2.
Align trimmed EV-DNA sequences against the indexed reference genome with Bowtie2 using default parameters.
Load BWA-MEM and create an index for the Leishmania infantum reference genome.
Perform WGS DNA alignment using BWA-MEM with default parameters.
Convert SAM format output into BAM format using Samtools.
Sort the BAM file by chromosomal position using Samtools.
Create an index for the sorted BAM file using Samtools.
Flag reads with low mapping quality score (MAPQ < 2) using Qualimap.
Create a new directory containing an HTML report summarizing the MAPQ for all reads from the sorted bam file.
Remove reads with MAPQ < 2 using Samtools to avoid false-positive CNV calls.
Mark PCR duplicates in the BAM file using Picard before performing CNV analysis.
Mark duplicates in the sorted BAM file using picard.jar.
Output a new BAM file with duplicates removed.
Generate a metrics file containing statistics about the duplicates.
Create coverage tracks in BigWig format using deepTools for visualization on an Integrated Genome Viewer (IGV).
Load Python version 3.7.
Load deepTools version 3.5.0.
Run bamCoverage with bin size of 1 base pair, input sorted BAM file, and output BigWig file.
Scale coverage tracks with scaling factors calculated from the formula: Scaling factor (S) = genome size / (mapped read pairs * read length).
Repeat the process for each sample to generate BigWig tracks.
Prepare an annotation file from the "chr", "start", and "end" columns of the genomic_window.txt file.
Set all "Strand" entries in the annotation file as positive.
Use the featureCounts tool with BAM files and the annotation file as inputs to generate a read count matrix.

Create a count matrix from BAM files using >library(Rsubread) >fc_PE <- featureCounts(files=dir(“.”, “bam”), annot.ext = ann, isPairedEnd=TRUE).
Extract the counts from fc_PE to get the read count matrix with >fc_count <- fc_PE$counts.
Use the read count matrix as an input in edgeR.
Normalize the read counts based on library size.
Calculate the library sizes for each sample.
Transform the read counts into Counts Per Million (CPM).
Filter bins with at least 50 reads per million in at least three samples.
Estimate common dispersion using estimateCommonDisp function.
Save the cpm_d50 data frame as a CSV file named cm_plot_data.csv.
Calculate the average CPM for the three WT EV samples and three Sb-resistant mutant EV samples for each bin.
Calculate the fold change for each bin using the formula FC = average CPM of Sb resistant mutant / average CPM of WT for EV samples.
Calculate the fold change for WGS samples using the formula FC = CPM of Sb resistant mutant / CPM of WT.
Inverse any FC value < 0 and then multiply by -1 to show the FC in Sb-resistant mutant EVs compared to WT on a positive scale.
Subtract 1 from all positive FC values.
Add 1 to all negative FC values.
Set FC higher than 4 to equal 3.5 for visibility of lower FC bins.
Set FC lower than -4 to equal -3.5 for better visualization.
Split the first column of the data frame into three columns: Bin, Chr, and Position.
Calculate the Position column as the center between the starting and ending positions of each bin.
Optimize the scale from -4 to 4 for easy visualization in circos plots.
Use the final data frame as input for the CMplot package.

Generate linear Miami plots for individual chromosomes using the provided code.
